AB-02.c01: Most heavy-duty vehicles use a **dual air brake system**: two separate air systems worked by one set of controls.
Inspect air brakes with the **7-step inspection** from Section 2, adding air-brake checks.
The in-cab air brake checks in **Step 7** replace the hydraulic brake check used on trucks without air brakes.
AB-02.c02: A dual system is **2 separate air systems** sharing one set of brake controls; each has its own tanks, hoses and lines.
The **primary** system usually brakes the **rear axle(s)**; the **secondary** usually brakes the front axle (and possibly one rear axle); both supply the trailer.
Before driving, build **at least 100 psi** in **both** systems; the warning shuts off above a maker-set value greater than 55 psi.
If the low-air warning comes on while driving, **stop right away**: front or rear brakes won't work fully, so stops take longer.
[CA] A **one-way check valve** is required between the compressor and the first reservoir, so tank air can't escape through a leaking compressor.
AB-02.c03: Air brakes add checks to **Step 2**, **Step 5** and **Step 7** of the 7-step inspection.
In Step 2 (engine compartment), if the compressor is **belt-driven**, check the belt's condition and tightness.
AB-02.c04: To check S-cam slack adjusters, park on level ground, **chock the wheels** and **release the parking brakes** so the adjusters can move.
Wearing gloves, pull hard; movement of **more than about 1 inch** where the push rod attaches means it likely needs adjusting.
Too much slack makes the vehicle very hard to stop; **out-of-adjustment brakes** are the most common roadside inspection problem.
**Automatic slack adjusters** are on all vehicles built since **1994**, but you must still check them.
An automatic adjuster out of adjustment signals a **mechanical problem**; hand-adjusting only hides it, so get to a repair facility as soon as possible.
AB-02.c05: Brake drums or discs must not have cracks longer than **½ the width** of the friction area.
Linings must not be loose, soaked with oil or grease, or worn thinner than **¼ inch**.
Mechanical parts must not be missing, broken or out of place; air hoses to the chambers must not be **cut or worn** from rubbing.
AB-02.c06: ★ items (applied leakage, low air warning, spring brake test) must be shown and their limits **stated out loud**, or the vehicle inspection is an **automatic failure**.
Applied leakage test: build to governor cut-out (**120–140 psi**), shut off the engine, release the parking brake, fully apply the foot brake, hold **1 minute**.
Maximum applied drop in 1 minute: **3 psi** single, **4 psi** for 2 vehicles, **6 psi** for 3 or more.
If the towed vehicles have no air brakes, the applied limit is **3 psi**; any bigger loss must be repaired before driving.
AB-02.c07: Fan off the air with the key on; the warning (buzzer, light or flag) must come on **before pressure drops below 55 psi**.
Large buses often warn at **80–85 psi**; on a bus, state the normal 55–75 psi range and say your bus warns higher.
A dead warning means you could lose air unknowingly: **sudden emergency braking** in a single-circuit system, longer stops in a dual one.
Farm labor vehicles and Type I school buses need **both audible and visible** warning devices.
AB-02.c08: Release the parking brake (and tractor protection valve), then fan off the air; the valves should pop out at normally **20–45 psi**.
On a tractor-trailer both the **tractor protection valve** and the parking brake valve pop out; on others, the parking brake valve.
Triple reservoir buses: if the valve hasn't popped out by about **20 psi**, try to drive forward; the spring brakes should drag.
Do the drive-forward test **only on single vehicles** with an isolated parking brake tank, **never** on combinations.
AB-02.c09: Run the engine at normal operating idle, typically **600–900 rpm**, and watch how fast pressure builds.
Dual system: from about **85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds**.
Single system (pre-1975 vehicles): from about **50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes**.
AB-02.c10: Static leakage test: system charged, engine off, all brakes released; time **1 minute** after the needle stops moving.
Maximum static drop: **2 psi** single, **3 psi** for 2 vehicles, **5 psi** for 3 or more, **2 psi** if towed units lack air brakes.
Memory hook: **applied** limits are **1 psi higher** than static in every row.
Parking brake test: seat belt on, parking brake set, pull **gently** against it in a **low gear**.
Service brake test: move forward at about **5 mph** and brake firmly; note pulling, unusual feel or delayed stopping.
